`ledger.mutations` is only ever appended to (line 117). Nothing prunes it on save, in `tick()`, or on restart. Every successful `save`, including each enable/disable toggle from the dialog (a fresh `idempotencyKey` per click), adds a permanent receipt, and this check is global rather than per owner. After 1024 saves in total across all principals, every later `save` from every owner and agent fails with `limit` (409). Users can then no longer create, edit, disable or re-enable schedules, and no in-product recovery exists short of hand-editing the durable `user-schedules.json` record. A single agent token that toggles its own schedule about 1000 times also locks every other principal out. The schema's `.max(1024)` is right for bounding the record, but receipts need a retention rule, for example per owner and keeping only the latest N or receipts newer than a TTL, so the bound does not become a permanent lockout. The tests cover receipt replay across restart but never the exhaustion path.

Reviewed by: claude-opus-5-5

Classification: backlog — valid availability/fairness issue, not a false positive. One principal can exhaust the global 1024 immutable mutation keys, preventing new create/edit/enable/disable operations for all principals. This remains an open limitation.

Recorded explicitly in RWK-20260928-sqlite-data-safety, dated 2026-10-03 note referencing discussion 4169151146: https://github.com/pioootrek/worktree-switcher/blob/main/docs/backlog/rework/RWK-20260928-sqlite-data-safety.json . It requires per-principal fairness and a bounded key lifecycle/operator recovery protocol covering in-flight requests, restart, restore, replay and disable-at-cap before broader multi-user acceptance.

The pre-implementation contract keeps accepted keys and fails closed at exhaustion. New boundary coverage confirms original retries survive restart, conflicting retries fail, and fresh owner/other-principal mutations are refused without deleting receipts. Focused run 88ee79df-ae35-4940-b7c2-31c6b10948db passed 54 tests; final full check 91517b7a-5abd-4c89-a847-0c832659cd3d passed 836 tests + 7 scripts. Blind TTL/latest-N pruning could replay a forgotten operation; no pruning/reset procedure is introduced in this follow-up.

When this deadline check fails after linkSync has already published the complete artifact (reachable in practice — the two syncDirectory fsyncs just above can block on a loaded host), the execution is recorded as failed but the file remains at execution.destination. Nothing ever removes it: the finally block only deletes the .partial staging file, and retain() only considers state === "succeeded" records, while the used quota calculation earlier in this method counts every ledger record of the owner whose destination exists, regardless of state. Each such execution therefore permanently consumes up to ~4 MiB of the owner's maxBytes budget; once orphaned files exhaust the budget, all future exports for that owner fail with limit, and there is no API, CLI, or retention path to reclaim the space (the README also forbids deleting the ledger). The same leak applies to crash-interrupted executions whose complete artifact is not reconciled because the deadline expired during downtime — with timeoutSeconds <= 300 that is the common case after a real restart, which the crash tests' clock manipulation masks. Either unlink execution.destination on this failure path, or extend retention to remove verified non-succeeded artifacts after readArtifact revalidation, and add a regression test asserting that a failed/interrupted execution with a published file does not permanently consume owner quota.
Reviewed by: kimi-code/kimi-k3

Classification: backlog — valid capacity/recovery issue, not a false positive. Complete failed/interrupted publication remains charged to its owner and success-only retention cannot reclaim it; sufficient such material blocks future owner exports. This remains an open limitation.

Recorded in RWK-20260928-sqlite-data-safety, dated 2026-10-03 note referencing discussion 4169216822: https://github.com/pioootrek/worktree-switcher/blob/main/docs/backlog/rework/RWK-20260928-sqlite-data-safety.json . It requires an explicit recovery/quarantine/reclaim protocol validating path/envelope/checksum/inode/aliases and durable quota accounting while preserving foreign/protected/unknown material.

New coverage restarts a complete 700 KB publication beyond its stored deadline: it stays interrupted/unavailable, the next owner export fails quota, another principal still exports, and evidence bytes remain unchanged. All three real SIGKILL publication boundaries now run within and beyond the deadline. Focused 54 tests and final full 836 tests + 7 scripts passed (MCP 88ee79df-ae35-4940-b7c2-31c6b10948db / 91517b7a-5abd-4c89-a847-0c832659cd3d). Fixture clock advancement simulates elapsed downtime; it is not a power-loss test. The existing uncertain-publication preservation contract stays intact; this review run adds no automatic unlink/GC.

On an already configured service, the documented `service install --refresh` path calls this parser with only `["install", "--refresh"]` unless the operator repeats every policy flag. That produces the default disabled policy; it is then passed to `buildServiceStartArguments`, which rewrites the unit without `--user-backup-enabled`, projects, scopes, or targets. `UserServiceManager.install` does not merge the previous unit, so a routine package refresh silently disables all user schedules and discards their startup allowlists/targets. Preserve the installed user-backup arguments when refresh omits them (or require the full policy explicitly), and cover refreshing an enabled definition without policy flags.

Classification: fix. Published in 8cd684de4646806c8cc6daa6fbe16eeb5b660e95; final head fa011f6972948d479ebf698ee8c629469c527222.

Refresh with no --user-backup-* flags now reads the installed generated argument array and revalidates/inherits that policy. Systemd quoting and launchd XML entities round-trip, including spaced/quoted/percent/backslash targets. Unsupported definitions fail before service mutation. Explicit policy flags replace the whole user policy; fresh/legacy installs remain default-off. README documents this.
